question.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{7}{12}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{x+y}{\frac{1}{2}+y} \\  & =\frac{2(x+y)}{1+2y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$

Now, substituting $y=\frac{1}{2}$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2(x+\frac{1}{2})}{1+2\cdot \frac{1}{2}}=\frac{2x+1}{2}=x+\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(x+\frac{1}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6})-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}]-{\mu }_{X|\frac{1}{2}}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-{(\frac{7}{12})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-\frac{49}{144} \\  & =\frac{11}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$
